# Endfield container differential fixtures

These synthetic golden outputs were generated by compiling the unchanged
`FairGuardUtils.cs`, `LZ4.cs` and `LZ4Inv.cs` from baseline `94318fa`, together
with `Oracle.cs` (only a no-op logger and fixture generator). Roslyn 4.11.0
from SDK 8.0.419 compiled them; the independent runtime was .NET 8.0.25
linux-x64. The original FairGuard source credits LukeFZ. The repository MIT
notice applies. Input/output lengths and SHA-256 values are in
`provenance.json`.

Basic FairGuard inputs contain `unchecked((byte)(i*37+11))`. Boundary lengths
cover the unchanged short-input path, the 32-byte header, the 160-byte branch
transition, uneven segment lengths, and both sides of the 1280-byte cap. Rust
compares every byte with the original C# outputs.

The literal fixtures choose only the first compressed length-header bytes
before decryption. The original C# reader generates the remaining payload;
its full compressed output and decompressed bytes are retained. The overlap
fixture exercises inverted token nibbles, big-endian back-reference offsets,
overlapping copies and extended lengths through the original decoder.

Reproduce by compiling the three original sources and `Oracle.cs` with
Roslyn `csc.dll`, referencing the .NET 8 reference-pack assemblies and giving
the resulting executable a net8.0 runtimeconfig. Run
`dotnet Oracle.dll output-directory`. Cargo tests read only the synthetic
binary goldens. Shipped executables do not execute managed code or require
.NET, and the fixtures contain no game data.

`endfield-clip.assets` is a separate synthetic Session integration fixture
produced by the backend's `quantized_complete_clip_fixture` helper through
`ASSETSTUDIO_ENDFIELD_CLIP_FIXTURE`. It exercises the Endfield header-mode
position and quantized dense field order through real application export.
It is not an independently produced C# crypto golden.
